record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures Associated with the Invariant Subspace Problem
record.original_question: Can a commutative algebra A of bounded operators on a real or complex Banach space be transitive while also having the Closure Property? Equivalently, is it true that every commutative operator algebra with the Closure Property has a common non-trivial closed invariant subspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a real or complex Banach space, and let B(X) denote the algebra of all bounded linear operators on X. A subalgebra A ⊆ B(X) is called transitive if it has no common non-trivial closed invariant subspace, i.e., the only closed subspaces Y ⊆ X with TY ⊆ Y for every T ∈ A are Y = {0} and Y = X. Say that A has the Closure Property if for every vector x ∈ X the orbit Ax = {Tx : T ∈ A} is a norm-closed subset of X.

Question: Does there exist a commutative subalgebra A of B(X) that is simultaneously transitive and has the Closure Property? Equivalently, must every commutative subalgebra of B(X) having the Closure Property possess a common non-trivial closed invariant subspace?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture in a list of open problems related to the invariant subspace problem. Web searches turned up no published resolution: results discuss related transitive-algebra and commuting-operator invariant subspace results (e.g., Abramovich–Aliprantis–Burkinshaw, Troitsky), but no source confirms a proof or counterexample to this particular conjecture about commutative transitive algebras with the Closure Property.

status_evidence.title: Some Aspects of the Invariant Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on transitive algebras and invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The invariant subspace problem and questions about transitive operator algebras remain a focus of active research, with related conjectures unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Invariant subspaces for commuting operators in a real Banach space
status_evidence.snippet: A commutative algebra of essentially real operators has non-trivial closed invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work has settled special cases of commutative invariant-subspace conjectures but does not resolve the Closure Property version.
